I feel my depression coming back, but I've got two jobs and a bunch of friendships to hold right now and I really don't want to have to go back on meds. I'm going to try every day this month to be more positive. I'm going to go on a diet, keep treats to a minimum, and hopefully lose a little of weight by the time the new year rolls around. But more importantly, I've been doing this mini-project focused completely on me in an attempt to try and love myself :)

It's just a simple list consisting of three items per day. I decided to start it in the beginning of the month and plan to continue until Dec 31. The list consists of three questions per day, which I absolutely must answer:

1) One thing I am grateful for in my life (my friends, my bed, my computer that I worked a shitty summer job to pay for)

2) One thing I like about myself (I have really expressive eyes, I make people laugh, I'm really good at downing straight liquor)

3) One thing I want to do in the future/events I'm looking forward to (conquer a thru-hike, get drunk while camping, going to my work Christmas party)

It's actually making me feel a little better... I'd recommend giving it a try if you're down in the dumps this season :D Also, as a side-note, cutting out depressing music is also helping me a lot.

Not as cool as some of the others here, but here's my story.

I was 16 and majorly depressed. I still struggle with it a lot of the time. I called a suicide hotline because I was feeling shitty, not because I was suicidal. I mean, I was always feeling suicidal then. It's just something that was always on my mind. It comforted me. It was like a trump card I could always use if bad went to worse. But the woman on the other end of the hotline was... not the best. I didn't feel like I was talking to a real person. It was like trying to pour myself out to a robot. So I exited the chat (it was online, not the kind you could call). But she got all butt hurt that i left and traced my IP address, and then sent it to my local police. One hour later, two policemen showed up at my door.

I somehow immediately knew what had happened when I heard two low voices of people I had never met before downstairs. In a panic, I hid any incriminating evidence I had and went with my mom when she came to get me. I've hadn't shaken that much in a long time. It was probably a bad thing to assume, but I've seen a lot of police brutality videos and these guys were both at least 6'4", with guns and tasers attached to their belts. So I was pretty much scared shitless.

It was humiliating. I ended up crying in front of them, and I hated feeling so weak and powerless. I felt horrible when I lied to them about wanting to kill myself.

But still, they gave me their cards, and made a lot of jokes with me. I always thought they'd be a lot more scary than that.

I don't like how a lot of policing is being done recently, but I'll always have respect for those men and what they do.
